title: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcan), Chichen Itza
summary: El Castillo, also called the Temple of Kukulcan, is the nine-terraced stepped pyramid at the centre of Chichen Itza, a Maya-Toltec city in Yucatan, Mexico. Geophysical work dates the standing pyramid to about 900-1000 CE, and it encloses an older pyramid. The city has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1988.

uncertainty.note: The authors give the date of the standing pyramid as approximate; the Exploratorium says roughly AD 1000.

as_recorded.value: dated approximately between the years 900 and 1000 AD

reviewer_note: Shape: stepped_pyramid (nine terraces, four stairs, summit temple). Height 24 m excludes the 6 m summit temple. Coordinates are the UNESCO property point, within about 0.1 km of the pyramid. Least sure of the facing stone; the opened papers say the infill is mostly limestone and give no facing material. Restoration dates (1930s) are from the same papers, not an INAH page.

footprint.description: Square plan about 55.5 m on a side with nine terraces and a stairway on each of the four sides; the terrace and stair geometry is largely the result of 20th-century consolidation, while height and basal extent reflect the pre-abandonment form (ISPRS).
